facts.text: Brutus was founded in 1874 when Abner Lee built the Brutus House inn on the Old Stagecoach Road, naming the town after his New York hometown.
The first post office opened the same year, with Lee as postmaster, making Brutus the first Emmet County post office not on Lake Michigan.
In 1882 the Grand Rapids & Indiana Railroad reached Brutus, prompting the town to relocate eastward to sit beside the new station.
Logging boom in the 1880s brought lumber mills, stores, and churches, turning Brutus into a bustling rural hub by the late 19th century.
In 2024 the historic Maple River Dam was removed, restoring the river’s natural flow and opening new recreational opportunities for residents.
